mathematical_checks.finding: Endpoint parameters are(c,2c,c,3c) with c=21/20. They are an admissible actual tuple, not the synthetic interval upperMatrix. Y=[1-q,(1-q)^2,p(q)], q=exp(-c*t), solves Y0_prime=c*(1-Y0), Y1_prime=2*c*(Y0-Y1), Y2_prime=c*(Y0-Y2)+3*c*(Y1-Y2) with unit input. The polynomial derivative gives c*((7/3)*q-3*q^2+(2/3)*q^4), equal to the third actual row.

q(0)=1 gives Y(0)=0. For t>=0,0<q<=1. The identities1-Y0=q, Y0-Y1=q*(1-q), Y1-Y2=q*(1-q)^2*(q+2)/6 have the correct signs. Y0-Y2 is the sum of the two nonnegative gaps. Continuity follows from the actually proved component derivatives.

The residual of the endpoint derivative over the actual drift, evaluated along Y, is R0=(c-k0)*(1-Y0)+k0*(1-u); R1=(2*c-k10)*(Y0-Y1); R2=(c-k20)*(Y0-Y2)+(3*c-k21)*(Y1-Y2). Each term is nonnegative under the actual upper bounds, k0>=0, u<=1, and the gap identities. This is drift domination along Y, not an assertion that the endpoint matrix is componentwise above the actual matrix.

The comparison matrix passed to differential_comparison is the actual fixed matrix M(k). For w=x-Y, the established residual gives w_prime=M(k)*w-R<=M(k)*w. This is the correct direction and avoids any need for a nonexistent entrywise matrix order. The proof does not assume x<=Y or use the desired bound as a premise; it also does not need an unproved positivity assumption on the actual state.

The four parameters are fixed outside the time quantifier; u may vary with time. hu requires0<=u(t)<=1 at every t>0. x is continuous on[0,infinity) and has the displayed derivative at every positive time, with zero initial state. The conclusion holds for every t>=0 and every coordinate. There is no hidden restriction to constant or monotone actual inputs.

endpointState_actual_solution packages admissibility, continuous trajectory, the actual ODE, the unit-input bound and zero initial state. endpointState_attainable explicitly chooses x=endpointState. Together with solution_below_endpoint this gives an attained componentwise maximum over the stated combined parameter/input/classical-trajectory family, simultaneously at all nonnegative times. It is not merely a synthetic supersolution with no admissible model witness.

scope_limits: The maximum is over all admissible fixed tuples and all permitted bounded inputs. It does not say the upper tuple maximizes the response for every preassigned time-varying inlet curve.
The certificate supplies an attaining tuple/control, not uniqueness or a characterization of every maximizer.

The phase2 decaying-inlet counterexample is consistent: for a barrier using that same decaying inlet, the gap inlet-Y can be negative. This module instead compares to a constant unit-inlet barrier and pays k0*(1-u)>=0.

The interface is for given classical trajectories: continuity on the closed nonnegative half-line and actual derivatives at every positive time. It does not prove existence for arbitrary measurable or discontinuous inputs, nor an almost-everywhere or Caratheodory formulation.
No time-varying parameter or coefficient-matrix theorem is proved. Pointwise residual algebra alone does not change the fixed-matrix comparison interface.

The uncertainty is the imported fixed rate-coefficient family, with inlet gain tied to k0 and the displayed matching diagonal losses. Independent uncertainty of physical volumes and water flows, arbitrary matrix intervals or a real apparatus are not certified.
No optimization functional or uniqueness theorem is defined in this module, but the upper comparison plus complete actual witness suffice for the stated attained-maximum interpretation.
This source review does not replace the recorded kernel run, undergraduate document acceptance, human testing, expert review or novelty certification.
